source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-60: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 60 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For Variant 60, first record assumptions and use a read-only diagnostic sequence before changes. Record GPU model and memory path, rank placement/topology, NIC/link/MTU, driver and firmware, framework/collective versions, transport selection, GPU-direct capability, buffer registration/permissions, message-size and batch distributions, and fallback policy; do not infer platform facts. Trace the operation from the application collective or point-to-point call through library scheduling, queue pairs, work requests/completions, registered buffers, NIC/link, and the remote host or GPU. Distinguish GPU-direct from host staging and identify the observable error that triggers fallback. Pre-register a falsifiable hypothesis, such as a specified change in end-to-end step or inference latency at a stated workload and uncertainty threshold; a device counter is not application benefit. Use a named non-RDMA baseline with identical topology and workload, warm-up exclusion, steady-state window, repetitions, clock source, compatible units, and percentile distributions. Measure end-to-end time, communication/overlap time, throughput, latency percentiles, CPU use, completion/error and retry/link events where available, and relevant device counters; correlate timestamps and report confounders. For diagnosis, compare healthy and failing ranks/links, check registration and permissions, queue/completion errors, counters, and application traces in dependency order, isolating one variable at a time. Test link or transport failure only in a controlled environment with bounded retries/timeouts; preserve correctness checksums or collective results. Accept the change only when the predeclared application metric improves without correctness, timeout, tail-latency, error-rate, or convergence regression across repeated runs. Stop and roll back to the last known-good configuration if thresholds are exceeded, completions fail, corruption is detected, or recovery is unbounded. Evidence required: versioned topology/configuration, paired measurements with uncertainty, correlated application/device/link evidence, workload/confounder coverage, and controlled fault-injection results showing detection, bounded recovery, correctness, and rollback. Redact identifiers, avoid credentials, and retain only approved telemetry aggregates.

Evidence required: versioned topology/configuration, paired measurements with uncertainty, correlated application/device/link evidence, workload/confounder coverage, and controlled fault-injection results showing detection, bounded recovery, correctness, and rollback. Redact identifiers, avoid credentials, and retain only approved telemetry aggregates.
